transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SRE); Sara Gupta (Hyperion VP Eng), Ethan Mercado (Hyperion Prod Ops), Priya Nair (Hyperion Security)

Summary (auto):
Quick review of last week's outage affecting Hyperion's inference endpoint. Discussed root cause (KV cache eviction + autoscaler race), mitigations pushed, and next steps for stability and compliance. Agreed on benchmark work and canary plan.

Topics:
- RCA and timeline
- Short-term mitigations and rollback plan
- Long-term reliability improvements (autoscaler, caching, graceful degradation)
- Security/audit artifacts requested
- Next-step schedule and owners

Action items (quick):
- Jordan to share benchmarks
- Maya to send postmortem doc and security pack
- Liam to propose autoscaler config
- Hyperion to confirm canary window

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hey everyo— thanks for joining, we're gonna go over the postmortem from the 3/3 outage. uh Sara, Ethan, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Sara Gupta: yeah thanks Maya. appreciate it. we, um, we've had the execs breathing down about customer impact, so wanted a clear timeline and fix plan.
[00:25] Jordan Patel: quick tl;dr — root cause was repeated KV cache evictions under a burst workload which amplified token compute and then the dedicated autoscaler raced and scaled pods out then back in, causing transient 503s. there was also a fallback misconfig where the model variant fallback didn't trigger fast enough.
[00:45] Ethan Mercado: right and to confirm, the outage window was ~18 minutes per our logs, but some customer requests saw higher latency for ~45m because of retries.
[00:58] Priya Nair: from security side we need to confirm logs retention and whether any PII could have been persisted in debug traces.
[01:10] Liam O'Connor: note — debug traces are ephemeral, we didn't persist user payloads to disk. they were in memory and ring buffer; we have the extraction logs we can share.
[01:26] Sara Gupta: can you walk through timeline again, because the sequence in your doc is slightly different than ours.
[01:33] Jordan Patel: yeah so timeline per our tracing: spike at 11:41 UTC, cache eviction at 11:42, autoscaler reacted 11:43 to 11:44, during scale actions some pods restarted because of improper readiness gating, so requests hit half-ready pods and returned 503s. we correlated with load balancer logs and client retries. on our side we had a fallback rule that should have routed to a lower-cost model variant but the routing policy had a mis-typed ARN — so it didn't match and didn't apply — human typo, we own that.
[02:05] Sara Gupta: okay that explains it. So the mitigations you pushed — what's done vs planned?
[02:12] Maya Chen: we pushed three things same day: tightened the autoscaler cooldown from 60s to 180s to avoid oscillation, fixed the fallback routing rule, and added a quick readiness gating for startup. we also rolled an emergency canary that redirected 5% of traffic through a pre-warmed pool.
[02:31] Ethan Mercado: the cooldown helped but we still saw a secondary blip during the evening run.
[02:36] Jordan Patel: yeah that was because the pre-warm didn't have the same KV-prefix warmup, so memory thrash happened when it took live traffic. that's why the benchmark work Jordan will do is to emulate the KV access pattern to pre-warm caches.
[02:52] Sara Gupta: makes sense. Priya — any more compliance asks?
[02:56] Priya Nair: yes, can you provide SOC 2 artifact and show KMS key rotation details. also want an architecture diagram that shows VPC peering and where logs are stored.
[03:07] Maya Chen: absolutely; I'll attach SOC2 summary and the KMS diagram. we'll also include the retention policy.
[03:13] Ethan Mercado: on rollback — if this happens again what's the immediate rollback plan? like, do you have a hot path to revert to hosted model?
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: we have automatic fallback to hosted variants, but that path is gated by account-level policy and needs a manual trigger for Hyperion because of data residency. for next week we propose a canary that includes a constrained hosted fallback for emergency only; need Hyperion approval on that waiver.
[03:40] Sara Gupta: execs will push back on hosted fallback because of data residency. we might allow it for <15 minutes but need audit.
[03:49] Jordan Patel: understood — we'll make that time-limited and log the event with the exact request ids.
[03:56] Maya Chen: ok let's go over the longer-term reliability items: 1) autoscaler tuning (graceful scale-in, longer cooldown, readiness gating), 2) smarter KV cache pre-warm and persistent pre-warm snapshots, 3) circuit-breaker for model voting and deterministic fallback, 4) better tracing IDs surfaced to Hyperion's dashboard.
[04:18] Ethan Mercado: on point 2, can you quantify the pre-warm memory cost? we have budget limits.
[04:24] Jordan Patel: initial data shows pre-warm adds roughly 8-12% memory overhead per pod for our model profile at 2k seq. we'll run more variant tests and share numbers.
[04:33] Sara Gupta: we need those numbers by end of next week.
[04:36] Jordan Patel: ok will do.
[04:38] Priya Nair: small nit — encryption in transit looks fine but we need confirmation re: log buckets and whether de-identification is applied before uploading.
[04:47] Liam O'Connor: yes de-id is applied in the collector. we'll show the pipeline diagram.
[04:53] Maya Chen: also wanted to mention we noticed a mismatch between Hyperion's burst pattern (many small requests) versus our expected median sequence length — that mismatch exacerbated batching inefficiencies. a possible fix is to suggest client-side batching or to tune our continuous batching window for this workload.
[05:11] Ethan Mercado: client-side batching might be tough, but we can look at SDK tweaks.
[05:15] Jordan Patel: we'll simulate both approaches in the benchmark suite.
[05:19] Sara Gupta: ok real quick — who owns the postmortem doc and where will it live?
[05:23] Maya Chen: Redwood will own and publish the postmortem in the shared docs bucket. Maya will send the PDF and a link to the logs bundle and the RCA board.
[05:30] Sara Gupta: good. and timeline to remediate critical items?
[05:34] Liam O'Connor: critical: fix fallback and readiness gating — done. short-term: autoscaler tune and pre-warm snapshots — aim EOW next week. medium: persistent pre-warm and circuit breakers — 3–4 weeks.
[05:50] Ethan Mercado: will hyperion want a test window? we can give you a 2-hour block next Tuesday morning.
[05:57] Sara Gupta: yes we'll confirm via calendar, trying for Tues 09:00 PST.
[06:01] Maya Chen: great. Priya any more security items?
[06:04] Priya Nair: that's it for now, just want the artifacts and KMS rotation log.
[06:08] Maya Chen: ok we'll send those. final q: do you want us to run an overlap test where we intentionally create a cache-miss storm in a staging cluster so you can see mitigation in real time?
[06:19] Sara Gupta: yes that would be helpful. schedule it during the canary window.
[06:22] Jordan Patel: we'll prepare the test harness and load profile; I'll share scripts and results.
[06:27] Maya Chen: recap of next steps — we (Redwood) will: send postmortem doc + logs link, share SOC2 and KMS artifacts, Jordan to run and share KV cache benchmarks by 3/17, Liam to propose autoscaler config by 3/16. Hyperion to confirm canary window and provide whitelisted IPs.
[06:45] Ethan Mercado: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:49] Sara Gupta: thanks.
[06:51] Meeting end
